meta: Two candle-stand panels of grotesques and vases by Agostino Mitelli, about 1650.
about: Two panels in the form of candle-stands are made of grotesques and vases. The right one has a base shaped like an octagonal block with rams' heads and garlands. The number 28 is in the lower right corner, and the number 27 is at the upper right of the left panel. Agostino Mitelli made the prints around 1650.

meta: A family finds that one of its members has drowned in a storm off the Isle of Wight, painted by Julius Caesar Ibbetson in the 1790s.
about: A family is in distress at finding that one of its members has drowned off the rocky shore of the Isle of Wight in a storm. A ship sinks in the wild sea under swirling dark clouds and lightning. Ibbetson had visited the island in 1791. He began his career by copying Dutch landscapes for dealers, and he is known to have made copies and fakes in the style of other masters.

meta: Edward H. Potthast's beach study of about 1910, the verso of a panel, from his New England summers by the sea.
about: Edward Potthast was born in Cincinnati, studied in Munich and Paris, and returned to the United States, where he began spending summers on the New England coast. There he studied the carefree seaside activities of bathers and picnickers. Although he never married, he was especially fond of painting young mothers and their children. This study was made around 1910.
credit_line: Gift of Virginia Rose Glidden and family and Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: A lioness lies resting against a steep background in Jan van Essen's painting of 1885.
about: A lioness lies resting in front of a steeply rising background. Jan van Essen painted her in 1885, and the Rijksmuseum holds the picture. Its note describes only the animal and the rising ground behind her.

meta: Anna Alma-Tadema's picture of her father Lawrence Alma-Tadema's study at Townshend House in London, 1880.
about: The study interior shows features of the Aesthetic Movement. The furniture is utilitarian, with a fur-covered couch, bentwood chairs, and a bamboo armchair and writing table in the opened-up neighboring room at the left. Tiles on either side of the stained glass windows and geometric-patterned walls are design touches often seen in England in the late 19th century. Anna Alma-Tadema made the picture in 1880.

meta: A circular fan by Ogata Kōrin with a scene from the Tales of Ise on one side and chrysanthemums by a brook on the other.
about: One side of this circular fan illustrates a passage from the Tales of Ise, a work of stories and poems probably written in the tenth century. Travelers meet a dark pass through the mountains and feel how far they are from Kyoto, and they say so in a poem about Mount Utsu in Suruga. On the other side white chrysanthemums grow beside a stream, painted in low relief with a technique called moriage. The fan is by Ogata Kōrin.

meta: A cow stands with her calf, tied to a tree in a meadow, in Jan Vrolijk's painting of 1879.
about: A standing cow with her calf, tied by a rope to a tree, is in a meadow. Jan Vrolijk painted the picture in 1879, and the Rijksmuseum holds it. The museum's note describes nothing beyond the animals and the tree.

meta: A hexagonal vase with a turtle for lid, handle and spout, plate 18 of Benigno Bossi's Suite de Vases, about 1760.
about: An unadorned hexagonal vase is covered by a turtle that forms the lid, the handle and the spout. Its tail curves down to make the handle, the spout pours from its mouth, and the cover is its shell with the legs sticking out beneath. Benigno Bossi made this plate 18 of his Suite de Vases around 1760.

meta: Hounds bring down a stag with a river landscape behind, in Abraham Daniëlsz. Hondius's Deer Hunt.
about: A pack of hunting dogs attacks a stag, with a river landscape in the background. Abraham Daniëlsz. Hondius painted The Deer Hunt, which the catalog dates to 1650, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A young man with a ruff looks straight out of a small oval copper panel by Thomas de Keyser from the mid-1620s.
about: A young man looks straight at us from a small oval. Strong light from the left falls evenly on his dark eyes and curly hair, his upturned blond mustache and trimmed beard. It plays over his black doublet with its split shoulder decoration and row of metal buttons, and it throws his shadow on the gray background at lower right. The swirls of his pleated white ruff frame his face. Thomas Hendricksz. de Keyser painted it on copper in the mid-1620s.

meta: Capri's rocky coast and the path toward the town below Monte Solaro, painted by Jean Achille Benouville about 1845.
about: Capri, an island south of Rome, has been famous since Roman times for its scenery and mild climate, and in the 19th century many European nobles and artists came there. Benouville painted its rocky coastline, with a path leading toward the town of Capri past the outcrop of Monte Solaro. He made at least three trips to Italy between 1838 and 1845, and after winning the Prix de Rome in 1845 he spent much of the next 25 years there. The museum says his style loosened once he left France.
credit_line: Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: A woman dressed as a man stands in for the bodhisattva Fugen in Kitao Masayoshi's scroll of the late 1700s or early 1800s.
about: A woman dressed as a man takes the place of Fugen, a bodhisattva who stands for learning as a path to awakening and usually rides an elephant. Petals falling from the lotus she holds teach the lesson that nothing lasts. The painting also alludes to the legend of Eguchi, a 12th-century courtesan who, after meeting the monk-poet Saigyō, revealed herself as a form of Fugen. Kitao Masayoshi made the hanging scroll.
credit_line: The Kelvin Smith Collection, given by Mrs. Kelvin Smith

meta: Two men play backgammon for stakes in what is probably a brothel's gaming room, painted by David Teniers in the 1640s.
about: Two men at the left are deep in a high-stakes game of backgammon. Three men watch them lay their bets, and another tallies the score on a board. The museum reads the room as probably the gaming room of a brothel, because of the young woman in the right corner among the men and the older woman looking down from a window. Backgammon was very popular in the 1600s and was often played for money. David Teniers painted it in the 1640s.
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Samuel D. Wise

meta: Saint Sebaldus holds a model church in a niche under four coats of arms, a print by Hans Springinklee, 1510.
about: The figure of Saint Sebaldus stands in a niche, turned toward the left. He holds the model of a church in his right hand and a baton in his left. Columns topped with globes flank the niche, and four coats of arms are above. Hans Springinklee made the print in 1510.

meta: An oil sketch of Rome with Saint Peter's in the distance by Pierre Henri de Valenciennes, about 1782 to 1784.
about: This oil sketch shows Saint Peter's Basilica in the distance. Valenciennes painted it during his stay in Rome from 1777 to 1785. The museum says its spontaneity and freshness are typical of his outdoor paintings, in which he tried to catch the light and atmosphere of Rome.
credit_line: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund

meta: Sophonisba writes her suicide note as the poison starts to work, in Pierre Guérin's painting of about 1810.
about: A Roman general seized Sophonisba as war booty, and her husband urged her to die with dignity instead of becoming a captive. She chose to take poison. In the painting the poison has just begun to work, and she keeps her composure uneasily while writing a suicide note. Pierre Guérin painted it around 1810.
credit_line: Bequest of Jacques de Caso in memory of Alice Cagliostro and Domenick Cagliostro

meta: A landscape with a canal, pollard willows and a farmer with a yoke, painted by Geo Poggenbeek in 1873.
about: Meadows are bounded by a ditch and a row of pollard willows. At the left a farmer walks with a yoke, and the church tower of a village stands in the distance. Geo Poggenbeek painted this landscape with a canal in 1873.

meta: Two elders threaten Susannah as she bathes in Johann Carl Loth's painting of the late 1600s, in the Getty.
about: Two lustful elders lean over the nude Susannah as she bathes in her husband's private garden. She thought she was hidden, but they had spied on her, and they threaten to accuse her of adultery if she refuses them. She shies away in modesty. The Getty says that when they later brought her to trial, the young prophet Daniel proved her innocent and the false accusers were put to death. Johann Carl Loth painted the picture in the last quarter of the 17th century.
